_: portuguese-fixes.json — the hand-edit record of the Portuguese (CAPLE) decks, applied by portuguese-fix.js AFTER paradigm-fix.js. See that script's header for the keys. Every meaning is the English Wiktionary (kaikki.org, read 2026-11-16)'s, shortened and never extended; `why` names the entry and the senses. Every added sentence is a Tatoeba sentence (CC BY 2.0 FR) named by id in its `src`, followed after “·” by how it was judged fit for a European-Portuguese deck: either it carries a marker Portugal uses and Brazil does not (named), or it is neutral — no word, spelling or construction in it differs between the two. Tatoeba does not record a sentence's variety, so no sentence is claimed to have been written in Portugal. A sentence taken OFF a card (`exDrop`) is one whose bolded word is not the headword, or which carries a Brazilian marker: a pronoun before the verb where Portugal puts it after (Eu me lembro for Lembro-me), pra, a Brazilian spelling (dezesseis, contato, gênero, idéia).

descSub: the six CAPLE decks between them teach 17 of the 1,342 here — none of which is repeated in this deck.

the six CAPLE decks between them taught 17 of them when this deck was made, and since November 2026 CAPLE A1 also carries ten everyday ones moved down to it (bom dia, por favor, de nada, com licença) — none of which is repeated in this deck.
The two subdecks are each ordered by how often the phrase turns up in a corpus of real sentences, so the ones you will meet most often come first.

Each subdeck is ordered by what a learner can already read: first the 253 expressions spelled entirely with words and forms CAPLE A1 shows, then those that need A2 (195), B1 (105), B2 (95), C1 (29) and C2 (31), and last the 409 that use a word no level cards; of the proverbs 28 are spelled with A1's words and most need B2 or more. Inside each step the order is how often the phrase turns up in a corpus of real sentences. So the Expressions can be begun beside A1 rather than after C2 — at the app's default of ten new cards a day, which with both directions together is five expressions a day, the A1 step takes 51 days — and the Proverbs are better left until B1. The app lists the two subdecks as two decks, so add the one you want; added together they are dealt side by side.

The cards are ordered roughly by how common the word is in everyday European Portuguese, so the words you will meet most often come first: the order comes from a frequency list built from film and television subtitles, with a reflexive verb placed by the verb it is formed from.

The first 79 cards are a beginner's first days, in an order written by hand: the greetings and courtesies (olá, bom dia, obrigado, por favor, desculpe), the words of a first exchange with the commonest function words, the subject pronouns, ten verbs, the question words and zero to ten. After them the cards are ordered roughly by how common the word is in everyday European Portuguese — the order comes from a frequency list built from film and television subtitles — with each closed set kept together: the days of the week from card 121, the numbers above ten from 201, the months and the seasons from 301. Words easily taken for each other stand forty cards apart. The greetings, the words e, o / a, a and que, five of the days, the months and three of the seasons were cards of no A1 deck before November 2026: 48 cards were added, 26 of them moved down from the higher decks and the phrases and 22 new, with meanings from the English Wiktionary and sentences from Tatoeba. That they belong in A1 is this deck's judgement. At the app's default of ten new cards a day, which with both directions together is five words a day, olá is day one, the courtesies take four days, the first 79 cards sixteen, and the whole deck takes 107 days; raise the daily limit in the deck's options to go faster. How the letters are read is a short deck of its own, Portuguese — Sounds and spelling, which is worth a week before this one.
